title: Systems Analysis and Design
description: Information systems and development methods; the business case, strategic planning and feasibility; project management with Gantt and PERT/CPM charts; requirements modelling and fact-finding; data and process modelling with DFDs; object modelling with UML; and development strategies, data design and system architecture. Built from the CSC 302 lecture slides (Shelly Cashman, Chapters 1 to 4); data and process modelling, UML, data design and architecture, which the papers test, are added from general knowledge.

topics.title: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
topics.summary: An information system combines hardware, software, data, processes and people to support business requirements, and systems analysis and design is the step-by-step process for developing it. Systems are built with structured analysis (the SDLC), object-oriented analysis or agile methods.
subtopics: Information technology and information systems
The five components of an information system
How business uses information systems
Structured analysis and the SDLC (waterfall)
Object-oriented and agile methods; JAD, RAD and others
The IT department and the systems analyst

topics.title: The Business Case and Feasibility
topics.summary: A business case is the justification for a proposal; strategic planning and SWOT analysis give the framework, and systems requests start the process. A preliminary investigation studies operational, technical, economic and schedule feasibility and reports to management.
subtopics: Business case and strategic planning; SWOT and mission statement
Reasons for systems projects; internal and external factors
Systems requests and the systems review committee
Operational, technical, economic and schedule feasibility
Setting priorities; tangible and intangible benefits
The six steps of the preliminary investigation; fishbone diagram

topics.title: Managing Systems Projects
topics.summary: Project managers plan, schedule, monitor and report on projects so they finish on time and within budget. Gantt and PERT/CPM charts show tasks, dependencies and the critical path, and risk management and change control keep the project on track.
subtopics: Project planning and identifying tasks; Brooks's law
Estimating time: best, probable and worst cases
Gantt charts and PERT/CPM charts
Task patterns, critical path and slack
Risk management, monitoring and reporting
Software change control and keys to project success

topics.title: Requirements Modelling and Fact-Finding
topics.summary: The systems analysis phase models requirements, data and processes, and objects. Team methods (JAD, RAD, agile) involve users, the requirements checklist covers outputs, inputs, processes, performance and controls, and fact-finding uses interviews, observation, questionnaires, sampling and research.
subtopics: Systems analysis phase activities and skills
JAD, RAD and agile methods (Scrum)
System requirements checklist; scalability and TCO
Fact-finding: who, what, where, when, how and why
Interviews: the seven steps
Observation, questionnaires, sampling, research and documentation

topics.title: Data and Process Modelling
topics.summary: Data flow diagrams model a system's processes, data flows, data stores and external entities, from the context diagram down through level 0 and lower levels. DFDs follow rules that rule out black holes, gray holes and spontaneous generation, and are backed by a data dictionary and process descriptions.
subtopics: DFD symbols: process, data flow, data store, entity
Context diagram and level 0 diagram
Leveling, balancing and decomposition
DFD rules and errors: black hole, gray hole, spontaneous generation
Data dictionary
Process descriptions: structured English, decision tables and trees

topics.title: Object Modelling and the UML
topics.summary: Object-oriented analysis describes a system as objects that belong to classes and interact by messages. The UML models it with use case, class, sequence, state transition and activity diagrams.
subtopics: Objects, classes, attributes, methods and messages
Advantages of object-oriented modelling
Use case diagrams; include and extend relationships
Class diagrams; generalization and aggregation
Sequence and activity diagrams
State transition diagrams

topics.title: Development Strategies, Data Design and Architecture
topics.summary: A system may be developed in-house, bought as a package, outsourced or delivered as a service. Data design uses entity-relationship diagrams and normalization to third normal form, and system architecture ranges from file servers and client/server to Internet-based designs.
subtopics: In-house development versus software packages and outsourcing
Evaluating vendors and packages
Entity-relationship diagrams and cardinality
Normalization: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF
File server and client/server architecture
Internet-based architecture; top-down and bottom-up design
